newsitem.title: GERMANY: World soymeal use in 96/97 put at 90.6 million T.
newsitem.headline: World soymeal use in 96/97 put at 90.6 million T.

text.p: Global consumption of soybean meal is forecast at 90.6 million tonnes in Oct/Sept 1996/97, up 2.8 million from 95/96, the Oil World newsletter said.

The independent publication said soybean stocks needed to be drawn down in response to meal demand and they were forecast to fall to a 12-year low of 21 million tonnes at the end of September, down by around one million from a year earlier.
End-season soymeal stocks were put at 3.9 million tonnes, down 800,000 tonnes from a year earlier.
Import activity in both beans and meal had been strong in the first half of the season in China, Europe and Mexico, Oil World said.
Future price prospects hinged on Chinese buying -- if it held up, resulting strong prices could discourage use in the European Union and other key consumers.
A slowdown in Chinese buying interest could help pressure meal prices especially as Latin American supplies were rising seasonally.
But low soy complex prices could encourage U.S. farmers to switch acreage to competing corn in the 1997/98 season.
